summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, morbid obesity, diabetes, and recent necrotizing fasciitis of the left lower extremity was admitted from an extended care facility after developing acute shortness of breath, chest pain, and hypoxia following a shower. He was transferred on empiric heparin for suspected pulmonary embolism after an indeterminate CT at an outside hospital. Upon arrival, he was stable and asymptomatic. A repeat CT angiogram confirmed scattered nonocclusive pulmonary emboli in the left lower lobe without right heart strain. He remained on intravenous heparin and was started on warfarin, which was titrated to 7.5 mg daily as his INR rose toward the therapeutic range. The surgical team evaluated his left leg wound with vacuum dressing and recommended continuation of wound care. He was discharged to the rehabilitation facility on continued IV heparin and warfarin with plans for hematologic and surgical follow-up.
